title: Play Mode vs Edit Mode: Unity-style transient simulation sandbox with save/load game flow and clean revert on stop

sections.what:
A formal separation between **Edit Mode** and **Play Mode** in the VirtualWorld engine and UI:

1. **Edit Mode (Default):**
   - The authoritative authoring surface.
   - Any edits made here (world painting, node placement, persona adjustments, trigger editing, or manual steps) are staged into the scenario and saved to disk on explicit Commit / auto-save.
2. **Entering Play Mode (▶ Play):**
   - Takes a complete in-memory snapshot of the scenario state.
   - Distinct UI status (colored topbar tint / "PLAYING" badge) signals simulation runtime.
   - Normal auto-saving to the authored scenario source file is suspended.
3. **During Play Mode:**
   - Simulation cycles, agent LLM turns, NPC movements, vitals decay, and event logs run freely in the transient sandbox.
   - **Save & Load Game flow:** Players can save their in-progress simulation playthrough to a named save slot (`data/saves/`) or load an existing save directly into Play Mode.
   - Any manual or runtime modifications made during Play Mode remain sandboxed.
4. **Exiting Play Mode (⏹ Stop):**
   - All transient simulation state (character positions, decayed vitals, inventory transfers, temporary memories) is discarded.
   - The engine restores the pre-play authored snapshot in one clean transition.
   - The editor canvas returns to the exact state it was in before pressing Play.
sections.why: Currently, running an autonomous NPC turn or stepping an action permanently dirties and mutates the authored scenario. Authors have to reload files or reset the entire world to undo simulation changes. A Unity-style Play Mode lets authors test behavior, prompts, and mechanics without contaminating their authored world files.

acceptance.text: Topbar displays a dedicated Play Mode toggle button (`▶ Play` / `⏹ Stop`).
Entering Play Mode snapshots `app.world.to_dict()` into an in-memory checkpoint and updates the client status to "PLAYING".

While in Play Mode, mutating calls (`/api/action`, `/api/agent/step`, `/api/soak`, ticks) advance the live world, but auto-saving to the active scenario file (`save_autosave(app.world)`) is blocked/diverted to a temporary sandbox save.

Pressing `⏹ Stop` discards the active simulation state and restores the pre-play checkpoint via `/api/saveload/restore_snapshot`, resetting graph positions, inventories, vitals, and dirty flags back to the authored baseline.
Save Game / Load Game flow works seamlessly in Play Mode:
"Save Game" saves the current simulation state to a game save slot (`data/saves/*.json`), not overwriting the authored scenario template.
"Load Game" can load an active game save slot directly into Play Mode.

Stopping Play Mode also reverts the event stream: the authored log is parked on enter, every row the run logged is discarded on stop, and the parked rows (plus the open turn card, counters, area log and raw-LLM chips) come back. Refreshing after Stop does not restore the run's rows from IndexedDB.
In Edit Mode, any change (manual character action, inspector tweak, or node edit) continues to mark the scenario dirty and commits to disk when the author clicks Commit.
Regression safety: existing tests and non-play routes remain unaffected.

files: app.py` - Guard auto-save during Play Mode
routes/saveload.py` - Play mode snapshot and restore endpoints
static/js/ui/play-mode.ts` - Client toggle controller and visual mode indicator
static/js/stream/stream-sandbox.ts` - Parks the authored event log on Enter and restores it on Stop
tests/test_play_mode.py` - Verification tests for snapshot isolation and restore

- Unit test suite created in `tests/test_play_mode.py`:
  - `test_play_mode_enter_and_status`
  - `test_play_mode_isolation_and_revert_on_stop`
  - `test_play_mode_blocks_scenario_commit`
  - `test_play_mode_autosave_diverts_to_sandbox`
  - `test_play_mode_save_and_load_game_flow`
  - `test_edit_mode_retains_normal_dirty_and_autosave`
  - Results: 6/6 passed in 2.33s.
- Regression suite passing:
  - `pytest tests/test_play_mode.py tests/test_saveload.py tests/test_scenario_commit.py tests/test_save_schema.py` (56/56 passed in 11.41s).
- Frontend compilation & tests:
  - `npm run build:ts` (0 errors, generated `static/js/ui/play-mode.js`).
  - `node tools/unit/run.cjs` (778/778 passed across all 57 test files).
- Event stream revert (follow-up gap, 2026-10-22): before the fix, a turn run in Play Mode left its
  rows in the stream after Stop. Measured live on `http://localhost:4477` with the topbar button:
  4 authored rows before Enter, 2 play rows visible during the run, and after Stop `PLAY ROW` was
  absent, `AUTHORED ROW marker` present, the stop marker present, and 5 rows (4 authored + marker).
  A page reload then restored `AUTHORED ROW marker` and the stop marker but no play row. Two
  consecutive Enter/Stop cycles both left no `CYCLE N ROW` behind.
  - `node tools/unit/run.cjs`: `tools/unit/test_play_mode_stream.js` 7/7 (park/drop chrome, fresh
    accumulators, idempotent enter, run rows discarded, no-op exit, discard, wiring guard).
- Zero em-dashes introduced across all modified files.
